this day, the c  the following:
 ORDER Heard on IA No. 22610/2023, an application under Section 301(2) of the Cr.P.C.
For the reasons stated in the application, the same is allowed and Shri Ramraj Dangi - learned counsel for the complainant and his associates are permitted to assist the prosecution.

The first bail application has been filed by the applicant under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for grant of anticipatory bail to the applicant who is apprehending his arrest in connection with Crime No.88/2023 registered at Police Station- Pathariya, District Vidisha (M.P.)
Kanchhedi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 15 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91365898/
1 for the offence punishable under Sections 376, 450, 294 and 506/34 of the IPC.
A s per the case of prosecution, prosecutrix, aged around 50 years reported to PS Pathariya, District Vidisha that on 09/07/2023 around 11.00 in the night, she was alone at her home.
Accused Ramkaran (son of the applicant) entered her home.
Accused Ramkaran pushed her on the ground and committed rape on her.
On the next day around 9.00 am, when her son returned to home, she narrated the incident to her son then her son went to ask Ramkaran about the incident.
Kancchedi (applicant) started abusing her son in filthy language and threatened to kill him, if he reports.
On such allegations, Police Station Pathariya, District Vidisha registered FIR at Crime No. 88/2023 for the offence punishable under Sections 376, 450, 294 and 506/34 of the IPC.
Investigation is underway.
Applicant is apprehending his arrest in this matter.
Learned counsel for the applicant, in addition to the grounds mentioned in the application, submits that there is no allegation of rape or for aiding in the offence of rape against the applicant.
Only allegations against the applicant is with regard to hurling filthy abuses and threatening the son of prosecutrix on next day.
Despite of this, applicant has been involved in the offence of rape with the assistance of Section 34 of the IPC.

Learned counsel for the applicant further submits that applicant had approached to the Sessions Court for anticipatory bail which was rejected, therefore, applicant is apprehending his arrest in the matter.
No criminal antecedent is reported against the applicant.
Applicant is aged 59 years.
Jail incarceration on false allegations would bring social disrepute and hardship to the applicant.

Therefore, the applicant may be extended the benefit of anticipatory bail Per contra, learned counsel for the State ably assisted by learned counsel for the complainant oppose the bail application for grant of anticipatory bail on the ground of gravity of offence.
Learned counsel fairly concedes that only offence punishable under Sections 294 and 506 of the IPC is made out against the applicant.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary and documents.

Considering the arguments advanced by both the parties and overall circumstances of the case but without commenting on merits of the case, this Court is inclined to grant anticipatory bail to the applicant.
Thus, the application is allowed.
